Partnerships
We believe in the importance of encouraging ambition, instilling a sense of self-belief, broadening horizons and inspiring students to realise their potential. Working with our local primary schools offers us the opportunity to share our resources and expertise, for the benefit of primary pupils and staff. These mutually beneficial partnerships assist in our unique transition programme, ensuring that all primary pupils enjoy an insight into what to expect at secondary school and a smooth transition into Year 7.
Throughout the year, specialist teachers and our dedicated team run an extensive variety of curriculum and enrichment activities, designed to supplement the primary curriculum whilst challenging their learning and encouraging the development of leadership skills, building confidence and self-esteem, and inspiring every pupil to aim high.

About the Department
SEND
Supporting SEND at La Retraite
La Retraite School is an inclusive school where staff are committed to supporting the needs and aspirations of all our pupils. We believe that all children have the right to a broad and balanced education, one which allows them to flourish and grow as an individual. Ensuring equality of opportunity and equity requires more than simply treating everybody in the same way, our aim and vision is understanding and tackling the different individual barriers and challenges a pupil may face.
As a school, we recognise the importance of not only supporting children’s academic progress but also developing their behavioural, emotional and social skills to enable them to become confident, independent learners.
I invite you to read our school Information report and policy which describes in detail how we identify pupils who have special educational needs and our use of the graduated approach to support their progress and development.
https://www.lancashire.gov.uk/media/922347/chapter-3-the-graduated-approach.pdf
We support children and young people with a range of special educational needs that fall under each of the four broad categories of need.
If a pupil is identified as having special educational needs, we will consider everything we know about the pupil to determine the support that they need. The support the school provides is then offered in the following steps:
1. Inclusive quality first teaching
This is the quality first teaching your child will receive from their subject teachers and may include some minor adaptations and differentiation to match your child’s learning needs.
All teachers and support staff hold relevant knowledge and experience to meet the needs of your child. All pupils who are on the additional needs register have a learning profile which is shared with the staff that teach and support them. This profile outlines their individual needs and the specific strategies that must be used to support their progress in and outside of the classroom.
2. Targeted, catch up provision
Specific targeted one to one or small group interventions may be run outside the classroom. These will be limited to a set period of time to minimise disruption to the regular curriculum. You and their class teachers will be kept informed of your child’s progress towards the learning outcomes of the interventions they participate in.
3. Specialist intervention
It may be necessary to seek specialist advice and regular long-term support from a specialist professional outside the school in order to plan for the best possible learning outcomes for your child. This may include for example educational psychology, speech and language therapy, occupational therapy and sensory advisory teachers. The school may need to prioritise referrals to these services. However, for a small number of pupil’s access to these specialists may be guaranteed through an Educational Health Care plan.

Our Mission & Ethos
As a Catholic school, our mission is to provide an outstanding standard of education for each of our girls, delivered in the context of Gospel values and the teachings of the church.
We are committed to delivering excellence in education which is complemented by an enriching offer that extends beyond the classroom. We aim to enable every girl to fulfil their potential, foster their aspirations and nurture their individuality and passions, to develop and celebrate every aspect of every girl.
Our Catholic Ethos in Practice
and to walk humbly with God
"To act justly" — We believe in treating everyone equally and with justice. Jesus was just in his dealing with the Jews and the Gentiles, and in this school, we strive to follow Jesus' example.
"To love mercy" — Jesus was merciful not only to those whom he loved but also to those who hated him. The merciful acts of Jesus are examples that we follow here in this school through our words and deeds.
"To walk humbly with God" — Jesus is the ultimate example of walking humbly with God. We believe that by loving God and others, we are walking humbly with God in the light of Christ.

Admissions
Admissions
If you wish to apply for a place at La Retraite, please name us as one of your preferences on the Common Application Form (CAF) and return it to your local authority.
The deadline for applications to your local authority is Saturday 31st October 2026. However, please contact us directly should you wish to apply beyond the deadline. National offer day is on Monday 1st March 2027. If your daughter is successful in securing a place with us, we look forward to welcoming you and her to our school and inviting you to join us on our highly successful transition programme.

Appeals
If a place at La Retraite is not offered to your child, you have the right to appeal to an Independent Appeal’s Panel set up according to the School Admission Appeals Code of Practice.
You must make your appeal in writing outlining why you believe your child should have been offered a place. This can be done via an email or letter and should be addressed to the clerk of the appeals panel.
All appeals must be submitted by Tuesday 31st March 2026.
If emailing, please send to mlove@laretraite.co.uk. Please make sure you include your child’s full name and date of birth in your appeal.
In-Year Admissions and Application Form
If you wish to apply for a transfer to La Retraite RC Girls’ School from your daughter’s current secondary school or because she doesn’t currently have a place in a school, please complete the online application form below.
You will also be required to contact your local council and make them aware that you wish to apply to La Retraite.
La Retraite will consider all applications. Once you have completed the application form, we will contact you directly. If the year group has space, a place will be offered. If more applications are received than available places, then the oversubscription criteria for the current admissions policy will be used. If the year group is currently full, the applicant will be placed on the waiting list.
The in-year application form can be accessed here.

Catholic Life and Mission
Catholic Life
An Outstanding school with 140 years’ experience in Catholic education (Catholic Schools Inspectorate Report, Feb 2024)
At La Retraite, our Catholic education is built on the ethos of "To act justly, to love mercy, and to walk humbly with God" (Micah 6:8). Rooted in the teachings of the Church, our school fosters a community where faith, compassion, and service guide our actions.
Our theme for the academic year 2024/25, "Demonstrating the Love of Christ through Acts of Service," reflects our commitment to living out these values. The Sacred Heart of Jesus, our Patronal Feast day, serves as a special occasion for reflection and celebration of this central theme, guiding us in our pursuit of justice, mercy, and humility in all aspects of school life.
School Prayer
O Jesus, through Your Immaculate Heart
my work, prayers, my joys;
my time with friends;
my difficulties, problems
I offer these, my gifts, to join
with Your gift of love for all.
Grant Your blessing upon all in our school community.
Click here to view our Prayer Card
Oscar Romero Award awarded to La Retraite
La Retraite has proudly been awarded the Level 2 Oscar Romero Award (Developer Level) in recognition of our ongoing commitment to promoting Catholic Social Teaching. This achievement highlights the many ways we actively demonstrate God’s love through creative, compassionate, and tangible actions across our school community.
Having now reached the Developer Level, we continue to deepen our efforts, living out these values with even greater intention and impact. We are now preparing to apply for Level 3 – the Innovator Level, as we strive to lead and inspire even more meaningful change rooted in faith and justice.
Our Commitment to the Community
At La Retraite, students and staff are committed to fundraising and supporting charitable causes. Over the years, we have raised funds for a wide range of organisations, including Trinity Hospice, CAFOD, Macmillan Cancer Support, the La Retraite Charitable Fund, Clapham Park Foodbank, Book Aid International, Handmaids of Mary Convent, Camps International (Kenya Expedition), and the Medaille Trust.
Supporting Trinity Hospice
Our work with Trinity Hospice has been particularly impactful. Mr. Phil Cuthell spoke to Year 9 students about the exceptional care provided by the hospice and its alignment with Catholic teaching on the Sanctity of Life. We continue to raise money each year for the hospice and work closely with a representative who visits our school to engage with students and staff.
Clapham Park Foodbank Collection
Every half term, we hold a collection for the Clapham Park Foodbank, a local initiative supported by churches and community groups working together to combat hunger. Staff and students generously contribute to these collections, providing vital support for those in need.
During the Christmas season, students take part in a shoebox project, creating gifts for children in need, which are delivered to the Handmaids of Mary Convent. Additionally, Year 7 students, alongside our Librarian, create Christmas cards for residents at a care home in Vauxhall where the Handmaids of Mary work. The positive feedback from the children and elderly residents is always heartwarming.
Form Time and Assemblies
Click here to view our Form Time Activities
At La Retraite, our form time routines and assemblies play a vital role in fostering our Catholic ethos and sense of community. Each morning, students gather in their form groups for prayer, reflection, and discussions that align with our school’s values. This dedicated time encourages spiritual growth, personal development, and a strong sense of belonging. During the month of June, students engage in activities focused on the Sacred Heart of Jesus, deepening their understanding of faith and compassion through reflective discussions and creative tasks. Weekly assemblies, led by senior leaders and heads of years, provide opportunities for Prayer and Liturgy. Through these routines, we nurture a faith-filled environment where students are inspired to live out Gospel values in their daily lives.
Liturgical Observance
Year group and class Masses are an integral part of our school’s spiritual life, taking place throughout the year. Year group Masses are held on Holy Days of Obligation, providing students with the opportunity to come together in worship and reflection. At the start of each academic year, Year 7 students are welcomed into the school community with a special ‘Welcome Mass.’ Our school feast day is marked with a celebratory Mass on the Feast of the Sacred Heart, held in the chapel, where students from all year groups are invited to participate in this important occasion of faith and unity.
In addition to the Masses, there are several other opportunities for prayer and reflection throughout the year. Staff gather every Friday morning at 8am for a Staff Mass in the school Chapel. During Advent, special services are held in the Chapel to prepare for the coming of Christ, and the school also hosts a Carol Service in the Chapel for staff, students, and parents to celebrate the joy of the Christmas season together.

Events
Throughout the week, we offer various opportunities for prayer, reflection, and spiritual growth:
Friday Morning Mass – Held every week at 8:00 am in the school Chapel, this Mass provides a peaceful start to the day for staff and students.
Student Chaplaincy Group Prayer – The Chaplaincy Group meets fortnightly on Thursdays during morning registration for prayer and reflection.
Year 12 Bible Study – A dedicated time for Year 12 students to explore and reflect on scripture together.
Confession and Prayer with Fr. Matthew – Every Friday, Fr. Matthew is available to support students with Confession and prayer, offering spiritual guidance and support.
Weekly Gospel Reflection – Each year group participates in a Gospel reflection on different days, helping to deepen their understanding of the teachings of Christ.
These events are integral to nurturing our school community’s faith and spiritual journey.
Catholic Life and Mission
Student Chaplaincy Group
The Student Chaplains have made significant contributions to the school Chaplaincy, demonstrating their commitment to service and faith. Over the past academic year, they played an active role in supporting the Clapham Park Foodbank through food collection drives and raised funds for Trinity Hospice by selling knitted Christmas trees, chocolates, and cupcakes during the festive season. They also received training as altar servers and have had the privilege of serving at several Masses. Before Easter, they were involved in selling Easter eggs to raise money for Trinity Hospice.
This year, in addition to continuing these activities, the Student Chaplains will be visiting local organisations such as the Clapham Park Foodbank, Little Sisters of the Poor care home, St. Bede's Community Church, and Trinity Hospice. They will also be taking on the responsibility of training other students to become altar servers.
The Student Chaplains also participate in gardening projects, fulfilling their role as good stewards of the earth, and raise funds for CAFOD during the Advent and Lent seasons. Additionally, they are volunteering to teach knitting to others. Each week, the Student Chaplains gather to pray, strengthening their faith and commitment to service.
Reflection and Prayer
At La Retraite, daily prayer and liturgy are integral parts of our form time routine, with members of the Student Chaplaincy group planning and leading these sessions. Students and staff are also provided with a weekly Sunday Gospel reflection, offering an opportunity to reflect on and respond to the Gospel message.
The Student Chaplains engage in various exciting activities, such as gardening and knitting. Those involved in gardening are also Eco Ambassadors, promoting environmental responsibility by encouraging recycling and maintaining clean, litter-free spaces around the school. Year 8 students have also established a prayer group, meeting every Tuesday during the second break to pray together.
Additionally, the Student Chaplains organise a 'Thought of the Week,' based on the Gospel, for students to discuss during form time. This provides a meaningful opportunity for prayer, reflection, and spiritual growth.

They’re worth exploring, but you can’t go wrong with the basic 'Bible' app. It will most likely be the first to come up and have the most reviews (as in roughly 1.14 million and growing). While it’s great to have a physical copy, the app can be an easy way to access Scripture on the go.
Religious Education at La Retraite
As a Catholic school, religious education plays an important role in the development of our young people. We provide a range of opportunities for students to develop their religious education, across each of the key stages.
Key Stage 3
We encourage all to engage as fully as possible with every aspect of school life, in the Religious Education curriculum as well as the worship and liturgy of the School. Within the School’s curriculum, Religious Education’s main purpose is to engage pupils in a systematic study of the mystery of Christ which we believe holds the fullness of the truth that God has revealed. We do this providing the understanding of the Catholic Faith in a manner that embraces ecumenism and inter-religious dialogue with other world religions and non-religious views. The students are invited, in a spirit of great respect, to be openly critical and reflective when engaging with the material.
We use a variety of teaching methods, from modern role plays, to games and music, as well as the more traditional methods such as reading, essay writing, presentations, and intellectual debates and discussions.

Key Stage 4
GCSE Religious Studies allows students to develop their understanding of the fundamentals of their faith and its relevance in the world today.
It generates a greater degree of understanding of the Scriptures and Church Doctrine and ethics, whilst encouraging open-mindedness, moral reasoning, and the ability to empathise through a greater use of case-studies, discussion, and debate. Students will also gain an understanding of another faith tradition.
They will be able to engage critically, looking at similarities and differences between Islam and Christianity, as well as other non-Christian perspectives. Students complete exams in a Catholic Christian paper and an Islam paper.
Key Stage 5
At Key Stage 5, we provide a range of extra-curricular opportunities and activities to allows students to build on their religious education from the previous key stages, and develop our students into well-rounded, faithful and considerate young people.

Why Choose A Catholic Girls School
Why Choose A Catholic Girls School?
At La Retraite, every aspect of school life has Christ at the centre. We believe that every one of our girls is made in the image and likeness of God and are unique and equal to others.
We wholeheartedly believe that our offer of an all-girls Catholic education can positively impact all of our students, regardless of their faith. The benefits of such are widely discussed and practised at La Retraite, as evidenced in our long history of success and outstanding outcomes for all our girls.
All-girls Catholic schools are praised for being academically exceptional and pride themselves on excellence, inspiring a higher level of academic self-confidence which encourages girls to pursue careers in traditionally male-dominated STEM fields.
La Retraite provides every girl with meaningful experiences and long-lasting friendships, in a stimulating and supportive environment that promotes values of kindness, compassion, community, gratitude and philanthropy. Our ethos encourages girls to develop as like-minded young women, who are inspired, ambitious and fearless with a culture that drives and celebrates achievement.
Our whole school offer, encompassing the Catholic ethos, all-girls nature, outstanding education, unique pathways and broad enrichment programme can enhance the lives of all girls and we warmly welcome students of all faiths and none, to make their mark on the La Retraite legacy.

Careers Education
La Retraite is committed to developing the whole individual and sees investing in Careers as essential to achieving this.
From Year 7 through to Year 13, students follow a comprehensive careers programme called 'Steps to Success', which enables them to develop the skills and attributes required for the world of work. Our programme complies with the Careers and Enterprise 'Equalex Model' ensuring all students are entitled to 10 days of experience of work.
In addition to supporting students with access to University or Apprenticeships, La Retraite offers a Scholarship Programme that is available to the top 20% in each year group, according to ability. Participation in the Scholarship Programme prepares students for Competitive University applications such as Oxbridge or Medicine.
We measure the impact of the Careers Programme through student panels, usage figures in Unifrog and destination data which we compiled each year.

The Skills and Post-16 Education Act 2022 sets out new requirements on the number and types of encounters schools will need to deliver for their pupils with providers of technical education or apprenticeships.
This statement sets out the school's arrangements for managing the access of providers to secondary students at our school for the purposes of giving them information about the provider’s education or training offer. This complies with the school’s legal obligations under Section 42B of the Education Act 1997.

Opportunities for access
Our provision includes various opportunities for students to access a range of events. These are mainly integrated into the school's careers programme and curriculum. These events are therefore delivered internally, with contribution from external providers where appropriate.
The school works with external agencies such as higher education providers including London Southbank University & Roehampton University, in addition the schools works with professional bodies to deliver workshops and engagement through the schools blended Careers and Personal development programme. LDN apprenticeships, ASK, Lambeth college and JP Morgan offer support to deliver engagement with pupils.

A provider, other than the school, wishing to request access should contact the Headteacher or Director of Sixth Form, via the school's contact details. Local providers are invited to key relevant events. In addition, external providers interested in coming into the school should speak to the Careers Lead. The details can be gained by calling the school's main switchboard or via admin@laretraite.co.uk.
The school's policy on safeguarding sets out the approach to allowing providers into school as visitors to talk to our students.

Gatsby Benchmarks
The Gatsby benchmarks ensure that every young person aged 13 and over will receive exposure to local employers in order to gain a greater understanding of the world of work.
The benchmarks also offer individualised information, advice and guidance around a range of post-16 education offers, from sixth form to technical college to university and apprenticeships, enabling young people to make informed choices about their future.
The eight benchmarks set out in the Good Career Guidance report serve as a framework for improvement in careers provision and have been adopted as part of the Government's Careers Strategy and statutory guidance for schools and colleges.

Cultivating Passion – Realising Potential – Committed to Excellence
La Retraite Roman Catholic Girls’ School is a collaborative, diverse and dynamic school, where innovative teaching and learning is the norm.
Firmly rooted within our local community, we pride ourselves on our reputation of 140 years of experience in education, a long history of academic success, high standards and an inclusive Catholic ethos. Every student is provided with a wealth of experiences and resources and equipped with the knowledge and skills required to fulfil their ambitions and make their mark in tomorrow’s world.
This constant pursuit of excellence is not only for the outcomes of our students, but matched for our greatest asset, our staff.
Recognised as an Outstanding School by Ofsted, La Retraite is underpinned by the commitment and support of staff. By joining our team, you join a team of dedicated, like-minded, passionate colleagues in a welcoming staff body.
Our Catholic ethos welcomes students and staff of all faiths and none, an eclectic network of partnerships enhances our offer to our whole community and a culture that is supportive and ambitious for one other forms our traditional, yet innovative school.
